work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim in the two code changes was checked against the code at HEAD (c23d2c9) rather than taken from the review: the two BUG-12 regexes still require a literal `="`, and the BUG-10 table still holds exactly one root-reaching spelling. Each of the four new table rows was derived from the same functions the table already exercises (beats/layerOutranks at :2819-2846, branchReaches at :2660, and two rows whose guard verdicts this file already asserts at :3742 and :3782), so the expected value of each is a function of code I read rather than a guess. What I did not do is run the suite: node_modules is absent and installing it would write into the repo, so the implementer's first act is `npm ci && node --test` to confirm the clean tree is green before editing. The three findings that are defects in text rather than in code (the PR body's Changed list, AC-20 and AC-21's stale baselines) are edits to GitHub metadata, which the finding names and this order can name exactly.
work_order.understanding:
Six follow-ups from the review and QA of PR #59, filed as it merged. I checked each against the tree at HEAD (c23d2c9) before planning it, and they do not all survive the check — the disposition is: two live code defects, one already fixed, three defects in contract text.

LIVE, and both reproduce on the current tree.

(2) The agreement table BUG_10_ROWS in test/web/pages.test.js holds exactly one row whose verdict can only come from probeStylesheet's ground-(b) half: `['html { font-size: 2.4rem; }', ['html font-size']]` at :3646. So the root half's only door is a single selector spelling, and each of these one-clause narrowings of the filter at :3378 leaves the whole suite green: `&& branch !== '*'`, `&& branch !== ':root'`, `&& !branch.includes(':')`, `&& !branch.startsWith(':')`. The h1 half has the same shape (its two real-override rows are both '#main h1', so replacing the reach filter at :3342 with `branch === '#main h1'` is also invisible). The review is right that both halves are at parity, and the asymmetry it set out to remove is gone — which is exactly why the residual is worth closing now rather than after it has shipped a second time.

(5) The BUG-12 test's two head assertions at test/web/pages.test.js:360-369 are `/<link\b[^>]*\brel="icon"/` and `/<link\b[^>]*\bhref="\/assets\/favicon\.svg"/`. Both require a literal `="`, so a declaration rewritten as `<link href='/assets/favicon.svg' rel='icon' type="image/svg+xml">` — same attributes, same order-independence, valid HTML, nothing a browser treats differently — turns the test red today. The comment three lines above them says attribute order in a tag is not significant and pinning the whole tag 'would go red on a reorder that breaks nothing'. Quoting is the same objection, and this file already has the quoting-agnostic reader: parseAttributes at :1714.

ALREADY FIXED — dropped, with the evidence.

(6) The QA finding that every page load 404s on /favicon.ico and logs a console error no longer reproduces. PR #59's own AC-24 added exactly that fix: the shared head template declares `<link rel="icon" href="/assets/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">` at src/web/pages.js:69 and src/api/routes.js:273 serves it, and the BUG-12 test asserts both halves for all five routes in all five states. A declared icon is what removes the browser's /favicon.ico REQUEST; a route at /favicon.ico would only remove the 404 and leave the implicit request in place, which is the argument written out at test/web/pages.test.js:342. The finding predates the fix and the review's own finding (1) records the same evidence. I have not implemented anything for it, and AC-5 below exists so that the drop is checked in a browser rather than taken on my word.

DEFECTS IN TEXT, not in code — three of them, and this order is the fix for two of them.

(1) PR #59's work order declared one file in files[] and said five times that the diff could not reach src/, while the diff is four files: `gh pr view 59 --json files,additions,deletions` returns src/api/routes.js, src/web/favicon.svg, src/web/pages.js and test/web/pages.test.js, +3306 -16 — not the '+402 -13' the PR body's '## Changed' list claims, and not the one file the order named. The order is gone; the PR body is not, and it is what a reader meets first. So the durable half of that fix lands HERE, and this order is written to it: files[] below names every file the diff touches, with no 'cannot reach src/' language anywhere, and qa_script step 8 is the opposite of the step being objected to — it tells QA to file what it finds, not to suppress a finding about a file the order happens not to touch. The other half is one line of GitHub metadata (step 4 below).

(3) and (4) AC-20's and AC-21's how_to_verify carry a 'today' baseline that the tree no longer produces. AC-20 promises that the coordinated '.page-title' -> '.pageHeading' rename gives exactly one failure, 'BUG-7: a pseudo-class is decided, not stripped'; at HEAD that test is fixed and the rename gives none. AC-21 promises that 'today each of the thirteen green cases gives exactly one failure'; at HEAD each gives none. QA is handed a work order and told to run these verbatim, so a green run reads as a phantom failure to file. The stale text lives in the #55 work-order comment and in this pipeline's ledger for a closed issue — neither is a file an implementer may edit, and I am not going to have an agent rewrite the framework's bookkeeping on a merged ticket. So the corrected text is carried as AC-1 and AC-2 below, in the one place QA will actually be pointed for this ticket, with the original sentences restated as the history they are. A human who wants the originals corrected in place is named in out_of_scope.
work_order.root_cause: Two different causes, and the ticket bundles them. The test-side cause is that the fixtures were written to pin ONE spelling per half of probeStylesheet: a narrowing mutation that still recognises the single spelling the table happens to use is indistinguishable from an honest probe, which is the same wrong-fix class AC-21 and AC-23 exist to shut. The contract-side cause is that the artefacts describing the change were written before the change was known — the files[] list and the 'today' baselines were true when written and were never revisited, and nothing in the pipeline fails when a work order's declared surface and its diff stop matching. The first is closed by adding rows that discriminate; the second by this order declaring its true surface and restating the stale text where QA will read it.

risks: Each of the four new rows is a claim about what BOTH implementations return, and a wrong `expected` turns the BUG-10 table red — on whichever side is wrong, which the failure message names. Two of the four are already proven in this file: `* { font-size: 2.4rem; }` is asserted to give ['* font-size'] at :3742 and `h1[data-testid] { font-size: 2.4rem; }` is asserted to give ['h1[data-testid] font-size'] in the loop at :3776-3789, both on the guard. The two @layer rows are not asserted anywhere and are the ones to watch: they depend on layerOutranks (:2819) treating an unlayered NORMAL declaration as outranking a layered one, which is what the existing row '@layer base { :root { all: revert; } }' and PR #59's AC-13 already rely on. If a row is wrong the table says so immediately and the row is dropped or corrected — the failure is loud, not silent.

The @layer rows depend on a direction that a future change to the cascade model could invert, in which case all three go red at once. That is the intended behaviour — they are the only rows holding the layer/root interaction from both sides — but it will read as this ticket's fault. The comment block added above the rows says so in the file.

Correcting PR #59's description is an outward-facing edit to a merged pull request. It is a one-block replacement, it is reversible with a second `gh pr edit`, and the counts are re-read from the API at edit time rather than copied from this order. The alternative — leaving a merged PR describing a four-file, 3,306-line diff as a one-file, 402-line change — is the finding this ticket exists to close.

This order makes two more numbers stale in the same class as the ones it fixes: #55's AC-21 enumerates thirteen green cases, and the table it enumerates now has 18+4 rows. No code reads that number, and the four new rows are all reporting rows, so the thirteen green cases are unchanged — but any future restatement of AC-21 should read the count off the table rather than state it, as AC-4's how_to_verify says.

No path in forbidden_paths is touched: no .sdlc/**, docs/**, .github/** or .sdlc/memory/** file appears in files[], and the PR description is GitHub metadata rather than a file in the tree, which is why it is a step in approach and an acceptance criterion rather than a files[] entry — files[] must not be a place a non-file hides. The app is not made to contact any host outside env.api_allowlist (localhost only, and this change contacts nothing).

alternatives_considered.approach: Take the review's fix literally: add one more ground-(b) row, '* { font-size: 2.4rem; }' or ':root { font-size: 20px; }', and bump the pinned count 4 -> 5.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The '*' row works and is in this order, but an unlayered ':root' row does not. ':root' is (0,1,0), which ties the class rule, and probeStylesheet's outranking chain hands every competitor index `sheet.length`, so it wins on source order and the h1 half reports ':root font-size' as well. The row's expected verdict is therefore satisfied by either half, and under `&& branch !== ':root'` the probe still returns it and the suite stays green — the row would pass under the exact mutation it was written to catch. A row only discriminates when the other half is made silent, which is what the layer and the specificity of '*' do. Adding the unlayered row would have produced a green suite and a false sense of closure.

alternatives_considered.approach: The structural alternative the review parked: assert once that each half of probeStylesheet's return is made non-empty by some fixture, so a future half cannot be added without a door.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Non-emptiness does not detect the residual this ticket is about. The single existing 'html' row keeps rootReports non-empty under all four narrowings, so such an assertion is satisfied by exactly the probe the finding describes. And the 'a half went silent' case it would guard is already guarded harder: BUG-11 hands the probe a stubbed [] and requires a NAMED disagreement on every reporting row, which is why that test exists.

alternatives_considered.approach: Close the root half only, and leave the h1 half pinned to '#main h1' as it was before this PR.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The review's own point is that the two halves are now at parity, one selector spelling each, and that fixing one while leaving the other reproduces the asymmetry this PR removed. The fourth row costs one table entry and closes it; leaving it would mean filing the same finding again in three weeks.

alternatives_considered.approach: Treat the favicon QA finding as a live defect and add a route at /favicon.ico.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It no longer reproduces: the head declares the icon at src/web/pages.js:69 and src/api/routes.js:273 serves it, and the review's own finding (1) records that evidence. The ticket says to check each one still reproduces and drop those that do not, and a route at /favicon.ico would remove a 404 that the browser no longer generates while leaving the implicit request in place. Dropped, with AC-5 so the drop is checked in a browser rather than taken on trust.

alternatives_considered.approach: Edit issuecomment-5848450143 and state/55.json in place to correct AC-20 and AC-21 where they live.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: state/55.json is the pipeline's own ledger on a separate branch, recorded by the framework's scripts and keyed by work_order_comment; an implementer rewriting it is editing the bookkeeping of a closed ticket rather than the work. The durable half of that fix is to state the criteria correctly where QA will read them for this ticket, which is what AC-1 and AC-7 do, and to name the original in out_of_scope so a human can still choose to fix it in place.
